status_summary: On 2025-01-24 the Acting Solicitor General moved the Supreme Court to hold briefing in abeyance in four pending cases so agencies could reconsider Biden-era actions; on 2025-02-06 the Court granted the motion in the Education Department borrower-defense case (No. 24-413) and denied it in the other three (Nos. 23-1229, 24-7 and 23-1067). On 2025-02-07 a Deputy Solicitor General told the Court in United States v. Skrmetti that the government's earlier equal-protection position no longer represented the United States' view while asking the Court to decide the case; the Court upheld the Tennessee law 6-3 on 2025-06-18. The Education case was dismissed on 2025-08-11 after a stipulation. These filings show the Justice Department reconsidering prior positions at the outset of the Administration; no source found shows the White House Counsel's role in those decisions.

timeline.event: The Acting Solicitor General files motions to hold the briefing schedule in abeyance in four pending cases (Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas, No. 24-413; EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining, No. 23-1229; Diamond Alternative Energy v. EPA, No. 24-7; Oklahoma v. EPA, No. 23-1067) so the agencies can reconsider the underlying actions after the change of Administration.

By orders of this date the Court grants the abeyance motion in Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas (No. 24-413) and denies it in EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining (No. 23-1229), Diamond Alternative Energy v. EPA (No. 24-7) and Oklahoma v. EPA (No. 23-1067).

A Deputy Solicitor General letter to the Court in United States v. Skrmetti (No. 23-477) says the government's earlier equal-protection arguments against Tennessee's law no longer represent the United States' position and that the new Administration would not have challenged the law; the government asks the Court to decide the question rather than dismiss.
The Court affirms the Sixth Circuit in United States v. Skrmetti by a 6-3 vote, upholding Tennessee's law.

Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas (No. 24-413) is dismissed under Supreme Court Rule 46 after a stipulation of dismissal filed 2025-08-08; merits briefing had been resumed by order of 2025-06-23.
